title: Dad Pete Joel (Chas McIvor)
style: country blues acoustic guitar warm baritone male vocal storytelling 106bpm walking bass brushed drums family portrait rugby lineage Australian honest character portrait unhurried
lyrics:
[Intro - acoustic guitar, wide open, settling]
Three men.
Same family.
Same game.
Different eras.
Same thing underneath.

[Verse 1]
Chas played
Because that's what a man like Chas does
He was built for something physical and honest
Rugby is both of those things
He went in, he came out
He carried it forward

[Verse 2]
Pete played
The middle one, the quiet strong one
The kind of player the team runs through
When things need to happen
Without announcement
Pete played
And the lineage held

[Chorus]
Dad, Pete, Joel
Three McIvor men on the field
Dad, Pete, Joel
First grade in the family blood
Dad, Pete, Joel
The game they all chose
Dad, Pete, Joel
The form they carry
Even when no one's watching

[Verse 3]
Joel played first grade
Which is specific
Which is not recreational
Which is a different kind of serious
He took it all the way
And the bounce of that
Showed up one night in a car park
When two men put their weight on his back
And found out
What first grade teaches

[Bridge - spoken, settled and honest]
Corey did not play rugby.
That's in the record.
He went to the ocean instead.
He found the surf.
He found the fire.
He found different fluency.
The family doesn't need one shape.
It needs everyone in their right form.
Dad, Pete, Joel — that form was rugby.
Corey's form was something else.
The family is richer for both.
Federation of commanders.
Each one commanding their own sphere.

[Chorus reprise]
Dad, Pete, Joel
Dad, Pete, Joel
Three McIvor men
On different fields at different times
Same thing underneath
Dad, Pete, Joel

[Outro - guitar settling, unhurried]
The lineage is intact
And Corey is at the ocean
And no one is less for it
The family knows what it has
In all of them
In all of them
